name: expense-cli
description: A long task built feature by feature (long-task workflow), judged by a hidden end-to-end test of the finished command-line program, the quality gates, and every feature marked as verified.

input.goal:
A command-line expense tracker in Node.js 22 with no runtime dependencies, run as `node expenses.js <command>`. Data lives in the JSON file named by the EXPENSES_FILE environment variable (default ./expenses.json), created on first use.

Commands (exact output formats matter: other programs parse them):
- `add <amount> <category> [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--note "text"]`: amount is a positive number with at most 2 decimals; category is one word, stored lower-case; date defaults to today. Prints `Added #<id>` where ids start at 1 and never repeat, even after deletes.
- `list [--category c] [--month YYYY-MM]`: one line per expense, oldest date first (ties by id): `#<id> <YYYY-MM-DD> <category> <amount with 2 decimals>[ - <note>]`. Prints `No expenses.` when nothing matches.
- `delete <id>`: prints `Deleted #<id>`; an unknown id prints `No expense #<id>` to stderr and exits 1.
- `summary [--month YYYY-MM]`: one line per category, alphabetical: `<category>: <total with 2 decimals>`, then a last line `total: <grand total with 2 decimals>`.
- `export <file.csv>`: writes `id,date,category,amount,note` then one row per expense in list order (notes quoted with double quotes, inner quotes doubled); prints `Exported <n> expenses to <file.csv>`.
- `--help` or no command: a usage text that mentions every command, exit 0.
Invalid input (bad amount, bad date, unknown command, missing arguments) prints a one-line error starting `Error:` to stderr and exits 1, without changing the data file.

Include a test suite run by `npm test` (node:test).
input.constraints: Node.js 22, no npm dependencies at runtime
